```{ojs}
//| output: false
// A one-time native "change" listener, not a cell reactive on exampleSelect:
// a <select> fires input AND change per pick, and two overlapping applies race.
applyExampleFromSelect = {
  const nativeSelect = (viewof exampleSelect).querySelector("select")
  if (!nativeSelect) return
  nativeSelect.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const example = (viewof exampleSelect).value
    if (!example) return
    VM.ui.applyExampleParams(exampleFieldSelectors, example.params, viewof plotTrigger)
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false

// inputs" once none does). Reads every example field's value so it re-runs
// whenever one changes; it only sets the dropdown, never a field.
syncExampleFromFields = {
  gText; x0; maxIterationsInput
  VM.ui.syncExampleSelect(viewof exampleSelect, examples, exampleFieldSelectors)
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Enter in a text field clicks Plot instead of submitting the field's form.
enterToPlot = {
  for (const view of [viewof gText, viewof x0]) {
    const input = view.querySelector("input")
    if (!input) continue
    input.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
      if (e.key !== "Enter") return
      e.preventDefault()
      viewof plotTrigger.querySelector("button").click()
    })
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Snapshots the fields when Plot is clicked (reads the stable views, not the
// reactive values, so it doesn't rerun per keystroke) and writes them back
// into the URL. Start from location.search, not an empty URLSearchParams, so
// parameters this page doesn't own (embed=1) survive.
committed = {
  plotTrigger
  const gVal = (viewof gText).value
  const x0Text = (viewof x0).value
  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
  params.set("g", gVal)
  params.set("x0", x0Text)
  history.replaceState(null, "", `${window.location.pathname}?${params}`)
  return {gText: gVal, x0: VM.expressions.makeNumber(window.math, x0Text)}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// max is always-live rather than commit-gated, so it gets its own sync
// cell instead of piggybacking on committed above.
urlSyncControls = {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
  params.set("max", maxIterationsInput)
  history.replaceState(null, "", `${window.location.pathname}?${params}`)
  return true
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
```
```{ojs}
// TODO: the method. Returns {rows, ...}: `rows` is the full iteration history,
// one object per step, plus whatever the plots need (the parsed function).
// Plain imperative code -- a while loop with explicit early returns -- reads
// best for this site's audience. Invalid input returns empty rows and
// `parsed: false`; the chart shows an empty-state message for that.
result = {
  const g = VM.expressions.makeFunction(window.math, committed.gText)
  if (!g) return {rows: [], g: x => NaN, parsed: false}
  if (!Number.isFinite(committed.x0)) return {rows: [], g, parsed: true}

  const rows = []
  let x = committed.x0
  let i = 0
  while (i < maxIterations) {
    const gx = g(x)
    if (!Number.isFinite(gx)) {
      rows.push({i, x, gx: NaN, error: NaN})
      return {rows, g, parsed: true}
    }
    rows.push({i, x, gx, error: Math.abs(gx - x)})
    x = gx
    i++
  }
  return {rows, g, parsed: true}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// TODO: what the plots share -- the rows visible at the current step, axis
// ranges from ALL rows (so axes hold still while stepping), a sampled curve.
setup = {
  const visibleRows = result.rows.slice(0, Math.min(Number(stepControl), result.rows.length) + 1)
  const xValues = [committed.x0]
  for (const row of result.rows) xValues.push(row.x, row.gx)
  const xRange = VM.plotting.paddedRange(xValues, {emptyRange: [-3, 3], relativePadding: 0.25, minPadding: 0.5})
  const sampleXs = []
  const sampleYs = []
  for (let k = 0; k <= 400; k++) {
    const x = xRange.lo + (xRange.hi - xRange.lo) * k / 400
    sampleXs.push(x)
    sampleYs.push(result.g(x))
  }
  const yRange = VM.plotting.paddedRange([...sampleYs, ...xValues], {emptyRange: [-3, 3], relativePadding: 0.15, minPadding: 0.5})
  return {visibleRows, xRange, yRange, sampleXs, sampleYs, parsed: result.parsed}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// TODO: the main chart. _plotDiv is a closure so the same DOM node is reused
// (Plotly.react after the first render) -- that is what keeps the reader's
// zoom/pan when the step slider moves. A hidden trace is not pushed at all.
mainPlot = {
  const Plotly = window.Plotly
  let _plotDiv = null

  return ({visibleRows, xRange, yRange, sampleXs, sampleYs, parsed}, showG, showDiagonal, showIterates) => {
    const data = []
    if (showG) {
      data.push({x: sampleXs, y: sampleYs, type: "scatter", mode: "lines", name: "g(x)", showlegend: false,
        line: {color: chartColors.fn, width: 3}, hovertemplate: "g(x) = %{y:.4g}<extra></extra>"})
    }
    if (showDiagonal) {
      data.push({x: [xRange.lo, xRange.hi], y: [xRange.lo, xRange.hi], type: "scatter", mode: "lines", name: "y = x", showlegend: false,
        line: {color: chartColors.muted, width: 1.5, dash: "dash"}, hoverinfo: "skip"})
    }
    if (showIterates) {
      // The cobweb: (x_n, x_n) -> (x_n, g(x_n)) -> (g(x_n), g(x_n)).
      const xs = [], ys = [], labels = []
      for (const r of visibleRows) {
        if (!Number.isFinite(r.gx)) continue
        xs.push(r.x, r.x, r.gx)
        ys.push(r.x, r.gx, r.gx)
        labels.push("", "x" + VM.plotting.subscript(r.i + 1), "")
      }
      data.push({x: xs, y: ys, type: "scatter", mode: "lines+markers+text", name: "Iterates", showlegend: false,
        text: labels, textposition: "top left",
        line: {color: chartColors.alt, width: 2},
        marker: {color: chartColors.alt, size: 7, line: {color: chartColors.halo, width: 1}},
        hovertemplate: "x = %{x:.5g}<br>y = %{y:.5g}<extra></extra>"})
    }

    // Keyed on the parse itself, not on the samples: a valid g whose iterates
    // run far out can leave every sample unplottable, and that isn't a bad formula.

    const layout = {
      xaxis: {title: "x", range: [xRange.lo, xRange.hi], zeroline: true},
      yaxis: {title: "g(x)", range: [yRange.lo, yRange.hi], zeroline: true},
      annotations: parsed ? [] : VM.plotting.emptyState("Couldn't read that function — check the formula for g(x)."),
      hovermode: "closest",
      uirevision: "static",
      autosize: true
    }
    const config = VM.plotting.config()

    if (!_plotDiv) {
      _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
      _plotDiv.className = "plotly-box-large"
      Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
      VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)
    } else {
      Plotly.react(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
    }
    return _plotDiv
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Declared above the chart block, not inside it: an output:false cell inside
// an .ojs-row/.ojs-grid still emits a zero-size node that takes a grid slot.
maxIterations = {
  const parsed = VM.expressions.makeNumber(window.math, maxIterationsInput)
  if (parsed === null || !Number.isFinite(parsed)) return 20
  return Math.max(1, Math.round(parsed))
}
```

```{ojs}
// TODO: the whole run, not just the current step -- iterate value against n.
iteratesPlot = {
  const points = []
  for (const r of result.rows) if (Number.isFinite(r.x)) points.push({n: r.i, x: r.x})
  return Plot.plot(VM.plotting.plotOptions({
    height: 260,
    x: {label: "n"},
    y: {label: "xₙ"},
    marks: [Plot.line(points, {x: "n", y: "x", stroke: chartColors.fn}), Plot.dot(points, {x: "n", y: "x", fill: chartColors.fn})]
  }))
}
```

```{ojs}
// TODO: error against n on a log scale, with the least-squares slope as the
// observed convergence rate.
convergencePlot = {
  const points = []
  for (const r of result.rows) if (Number.isFinite(r.error) && r.error > 0) points.push({n: r.i, error: r.error})
  const fitInput = []
  for (const p of points) fitInput.push({x: p.n, y: Math.log10(p.error)})
  const fit = VM.numerical.linearRegression(fitInput)
  const marks = [Plot.line(points, {x: "n", y: "error", stroke: chartColors.alt}), Plot.dot(points, {x: "n", y: "error", fill: chartColors.alt})]
  if (fit) {
    marks.push(Plot.line([{n: fit.xlo, error: 10 ** (fit.slope * fit.xlo + fit.intercept)}, {n: fit.xhi, error: 10 ** (fit.slope * fit.xhi + fit.intercept)}],
      {x: "n", y: "error", stroke: chartColors.muted, strokeDasharray: "4 3"}))
  }
  return Plot.plot(VM.plotting.plotOptions({
    height: 260,
    x: {label: "n"},
    y: {label: "|xₙ₊₁ − xₙ|", type: "log"},
    marks
  }))
}
```

```{ojs}
// TODO: the raw run. Always return a Node, even when empty, so Quarto's OJS
// runtime never latches this cell as hidden.
iterationTable = {
  if (result.rows.length === 0) return document.createElement("div")
  const formattedRows = []
  for (const row of result.rows) {
    let xCell = "NaN"
    if (Number.isFinite(row.x)) xCell = row.x.toPrecision(10)
    let gxCell = "NaN"
    if (Number.isFinite(row.gx)) gxCell = row.gx.toPrecision(10)
    let errorCell = "NaN"
    if (Number.isFinite(row.error)) errorCell = row.error.toExponential(4)
    formattedRows.push([row.i, xCell, gxCell, errorCell])
  }
  return VM.ui.renderTable({
    html,
    headers: ["n", tex`x_n`, tex`g(x_n)`, tex`|x_{n+1} - x_n|`],
    csvHeaders: ["n", "x_n", "g(x_n)", "|x_{n+1} - x_n|"],
    filename: "TODO-method-iterations.csv",
    rows: formattedRows
  })
}
```

TODO: the explanation. What the method does, the update rule as a display
equation, when it converges and how fast, and what to try in the app above.
Fixed-point iteration solves $x = g(x)$ by repeating

$$
x_{n+1} = g(x_n),
$$

which converges to a fixed point $x^*$ whenever $|g'(x^*)| < 1$ and $x_0$ is
close enough -- linearly, with ratio $|g'(x^*)|$.
